title: Two Kepler sampling tests show that a smooth dip baseline can create a false periodic loss response
abstract: We test whether the known 0.88-day signal weakens during two deep dips of KIC 8462852. A fit with a cubic spline baseline and loss-times-harmonic terms gives large response coefficients that change with the baseline. We test the method with symmetric Gaussian dips plus a constant 90-ppm signal on the same Kepler quarter 8 and quarter 16 time grids. For a 0.25-day Gaussian width and 0.40-day spline knots, the fitted false response norms are about 221224 and 204405 ppm per unit loss. The true response is zero. Separate linear projections show that the dip supplies the false response. Thus small residual-block errors do not make these fits valid source measurements. This result concerns the tested baseline and selected sampling. It does not locate the periodic source, test all attenuation methods, or overturn the published blend argument. No new source or planet is found. The bundle contains original code, aggregate results, source hashes, figures and separate-scratch reproduction steps.
